payload.title: ROOT CAUSE FOUND — the cycle-snapshot cache is structurally unhittable: writer keys the filename on RAW wall clock, reader is specified to key it on ROUNDED wall clock, sampled later
payload.supersedes: 6 ticks of my own reporting that framed this as 'cycle_snapshot_promoted:false' / 'named by wall clock, looked up by nominal tick'. Both framings were incomplete and the second was wrong about the reader.

mechanism.writer: docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 — FILE_TICK=$(date -u +%H:%M), RAW dispatcher wall clock, no quantization. Also passes --arg tick "$FILE_TICK" so the in-file .tick field carries the same raw value.
mechanism.reader: .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1 — 'TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot)', i.e. QUANTIZED, and sampled at the AGENT's own clock which is later than the dispatcher's by the spawn+startup latency.
mechanism.consequence: The two sides use different quantization AND different sampling instants. They can only agree by coincidence.

live_reproduction_this_tick.agent_quote: No exact tick-snapshot match for cycle-snapshot-07:22.json -> direct get_cycle_bootstrap + get_macro_snapshot + get_macro_calendar
live_reproduction_this_tick.note: The file WAS on disk and WAS fresh (2 min old, inside the SKILL's 7-minute window). Had the agent applied the SKILL's own rounding, 07:22 -> 07:20 would have HIT. So this tick stacked TWO independent failures.

two_independent_failures.implication: Even a reader that follows the SKILL's rounding correctly can only ever hit the ~32% of files that happen to land on a boundary — and only if its rounded minute equals the writer's raw minute AND the file is <7 min old.

two_independent_failures.severity: spec ambiguity, not obviously agent fault
two_independent_failures.evidence: alert-commander used the raw 07:22. The SKILL's rounding rule is illustrated with the single example '02:05 -> "02:05"' — a no-op that does not exercise rounding at all, so the parenthetical is easy to read as decorative next to the primary 'formatted as HH:MM'.
two_independent_failures.implication: Fix the example alongside any rounding fix, or the next reader repeats it.

why_this_went_unnoticed_for_6_ticks.cause: .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md still states: 'The snapshot writer (cowork-team dispatcher) is a future task. Until it lands, Step -1 will always miss and fall through to Step 0 — zero behavior regression.'
why_this_went_unnoticed_for_6_ticks.problem: The writer HAS landed (Step 4.7 is live and ran on every non-silent tick today). That note tells every reading agent the miss is EXPECTED and harmless, so no agent has ever escalated it. The stale doc is what suppressed the signal.
why_this_went_unnoticed_for_6_ticks.note: This stale line was already on my agent-father brief as a minor doc-hygiene item. It is not minor — it is the reason the defect is 6+ ticks old and unreported.

payload.measured_cost: Step 4.7's stated purpose is 'Agents read this file instead of calling get_cycle_bootstrap independently.' Today it costs 2 MCP round trips + a ~16KB write per non-silent tick, and the agent then makes those same calls anyway. Waste on both sides, zero benefit. Confirmed this tick: alert-commander fell through to get_cycle_bootstrap + get_macro_snapshot + get_macro_calendar.

recommended_fix.direction: Delete BOTH wall clocks. Key the snapshot on the NOMINAL tick and have the reader derive the identical key from the scheduled_utc token the dispatcher already passes it.
recommended_fix.why_this_shape: spawn-fanout.md already appends 'scheduled_utc=<ISO8601>' to every spawn prompt, and it demonstrably arrives and is used — chef's marker this tick was published:chef-intraday:2026-08-25:14, whose date part came from scheduled_utc=2026-08-25T07:13:00.000Z, not from a date -u call.
recommended_fix.precedent: This is exactly the class FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-ANCHOR-3 already solved: 'the worker never re-reads the wall clock to derive its own window key'. Same defect, different key. Apply the same remedy.
recommended_fix.also_required: Delete or correct the 'writer is a future task' note in cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md, and replace the no-op rounding example.
recommended_fix.caution: A rename-only fix is NOT sufficient — the fence also writes the raw value into the in-file .tick field via --arg tick "$FILE_TICK", so any content-based lookup would still miss.

payload.owner_hint: architect — this spans the dispatcher fence, a shared skill consumed by 8 agents, and the spawn-prompt contract. Not a single-file doc edit.
payload.dispatcher_note: Executed Step 4.7 verbatim again this tick rather than hand-substituting a nominal tick. Hand-correcting would be an unrecorded flow edit and would have destroyed the 28-of-41 off-boundary evidence that identified W1.
